expectations.text: Identifies that routes.ts performs data-access and/or business branching that belongs in the service
expectations.evidence: Finding 3 (High), 'routes.ts:6,28,33-46 — the route owns the business logic and talks to the repository directly': quotes line 28 `const repo = new DigestsRepository(app.container.db)`, line 36 `repo.findByPeriod`, line 38 the `if (existing && !req.body.regenerate)` branch, line 42 `repo.deleteById`, and states 'Everything the digest feature actually decides — what the period window is, whether a cached digest counts, whether to rebuild, and the delete-then-rebuild sequencing — lives in the handler.' Fix proposes collapsing lines 33-47 into one service call and dropping the repository import. Matches planted V1.1 exactly, including the line set 28/36/38/43/52 (line 52 covered by 'GET /digests should likewise call service.list').

expectations.text: Identifies that service.ts queries the database directly instead of going through the repository
expectations.evidence: Finding 2 (Critical), 'service.ts:1,5,26–56 — the service issues raw Drizzle queries instead of going through a repository': quotes line 5 `import * as t from '../../db/schema.js'`, line 26 and line 51 `this.container.db.select(...)`. States 'The digests service already constructs a DigestsRepository on line 22 and then reaches past it.' Fix: move both queries onto DigestsRepository. Matches planted V1.2 (lines 5, 26, 51).

expectations.text: Identifies that service.ts constructs the concrete OctokitGitHubClient adapter instead of resolving it from the container
expectations.evidence: Finding 1 (Critical), 'service.ts:2,58 — the service imports and constructs a concrete adapter, and reads the token from process.env': quotes line 2 `import { OctokitGitHubClient } from '../../adapters/github/octokit.js'` and line 58 `new OctokitGitHubClient(process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN ?? '')`. Names it a composition-root violation and a SecretsProvider bypass; fix is `await this.container.github()`. Matches planted V1.3 (lines 2, 58) including the secrets half of the rule.

This is the documented, intentional compromise in guides/pitfalls-and-tradeoffs.md — not a finding.' Appears nowhere in the numbered findings.

expectations.text: Does NOT flag the row-type-as-DTO pattern as a defect
expectations.evidence: Explicitly CLEARED: '**DigestRow = typeof t.digests.$inferSelect in repository.ts:5.** Row-types-as-DTOs is an accepted trade-off here; keeping it in the owning repository rather than db/rows.ts is correct while digests has no cross-cutting consumer.' Finding 15 does mention 'the route returns the raw row' but its substance is a genuine, separate defect — periodStart/periodEnd/bodyMd are nullable in db/schema/ops.ts:46-48, NULLs sort first under `orderBy(desc(...))`, and the unrelated `deliveredTo` column leaks. It does not assert that row types must be replaced by a hand-modelled domain-entity layer, and the pattern itself is explicitly named as accepted. Graded as cleared, not flagged. (Recorded in eval_feedback as borderline.)

suggestions.assertion: Does NOT flag the row-type-as-DTO pattern as a defect
suggestions.reason: Borderline, recorded verbatim per GRADING.md. This run clears the decoy outright ('Row-types-as-DTOs is an accepted trade-off here') but its Low finding 15 still says 'the route returns the raw row — including the unrelated deliveredTo column — with no response schema' and proposes to 'shape a small DTO in the route'. The decoy would be sharper if the fixture's digests columns were NOT nullable — as written, a reviewer has a genuine null-safety reason to touch the response shape, which muddies the signal the assertion is trying to read.

suggestions.assertion: Every reported problem cites a specific file and line
suggestions.reason: Non-discriminating as written: all four runs anchor essentially every code finding to file:line, and all four contain the same unanchorable 'no tests ship with this module' finding. The assertion cannot separate a good review from a bad one here. Consider narrowing it to 'every finding about code present in the fixture cites file and line' or dropping it.

Prominence, which GRADING.md rightly excludes from the verdict, is worth capturing as a separate metric: this run ranks the two Dependency-Rule violations as its top two Critical findings and the route-layer violation as High #3, i.e. all three planted defects are in the first three positions. Nothing in the assertion set rewards that.

eval_feedback.overall: All three planted violations detected and ranked at the top; both decoys explicitly cleared in a dedicated 'do not fix these' section. The only assertion that gave me pause was the row-type-as-DTO decoy, where an adjacent nullable-column finding proposes response shaping.
